questions.stem: Which one of the following statements is <u>incorrect</u>?

options.A: History helps us to be proud of our culture and national identity.
options.B: The period before writing was developed is known as pre-history.
options.C: History can be written without a source.
options.D: Letters, treaties, tools and paintings are examples of primary sources.
options.E: Primary sources are firsthand accounts of an event.

explanation_steps: The textbook: 'A source is the material out of which history is written. No history can be written without a source.'
A, B, D and E are all statements from Unit 1 (importance of history, pre-history, primary sources).
So C is the incorrect statement. Answer: C.
tips: 'Incorrect' questions: test each option against the textbook; the one that contradicts it is the answer.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is a secondary source?

options.B: A letter written by a soldier

explanation_steps: Primary sources come from the period itself; later interpretations are secondary.
A modern textbook is secondary. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which of the following people had a calendar of 12 months and 30 days each?
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The Babylonians were probably the first people to develop a calendar. They had a lunar calendar of 12 months of 30 days each.'
It then says the Egyptian solar calendar had 365 days, 'divided into 12 months of 30 days each and 5 extra days at the end'.
The wording of the question matches the Babylonian calendar exactly, but the Egyptian calendar also had 12 months of 30 days (+5 days).
Keyed B (Babylonians); A (Egyptians) is also accepted.
tips: Babylonians: lunar, 12 × 30 = 360 days. Egyptians: solar, 12 × 30 + 5 = 365 days. Greeks: lunisolar 354 days. Julius Caesar: Julian calendar.

similar_questions.stem: The calendar of 365 days made of 12 months of 30 days plus 5 extra days was the calendar of the:
explanation_steps: The Egyptians replaced the lunar calendar with a solar one: 12 × 30 + 5 = 365 days.
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.section: 1.4 Dating Time in History – calendars

questions.review_flag: Two defensible options: the textbook gives both the Babylonians (lunar calendar of 12 months of 30 days) and the Egyptians (12 months of 30 days + 5 extra days). Keyed B because the stem copies the Babylonian sentence; A accepted. Teacher decision.

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>was not</u> true of Hammurabi’s Laws?

options.A: Women had fewer rights and their place was in the home.
options.C: Children were to obey their fathers.
options.D: If a woman failed to bear children, her husband could divorce her.
options.E: Women had equal rights with men.

explanation_steps: The textbook: Mesopotamian society was patriarchal (dominated by men); in the family Hammurabi's code gave women fewer rights and their place was in the home.
A husband could divorce a wife who failed to bear children, and children had to obey their fathers.
So 'women had equal rights with men' was NOT true. Answer: E.
tips: Patriarchal = male-dominated: any option saying women were equal is the odd one out.

similar_questions.stem: Hammurabi's code was based on the principle of:

options.B: equal retaliation ('an eye for an eye')

explanation_steps: Hammurabi's laws followed equal retaliation – punishment matching the crime.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Find the sentence which <u>is not</u> true.

options.A: Hinduism believes in the idea of reincarnation.
options.B: According to the teachings of Buddha, life is full of suffering.
options.C: Buddha teaches that people should not kill and should not steal.
options.D: The most important religious practice of Buddha is yoga or meditation.
options.E: Hinduism has created a legacy of equality in Indian societies.

explanation_steps: The textbook: 'By stressing caste division, Hinduism has created a legacy of inequality which still survives in Indian society.'
A–D are all textbook statements (reincarnation; first Noble Truth 'life is full of suffering'; 'the most important religious practice of Buddhism is yoga or meditation').
E replaces 'inequality' with 'equality', so it is false. Answer: E.
tips: Watch for one changed word (inequality → equality).

questions.stem: One of the following <u>was not</u> included in Confucius’s teachings.

options.A: Governments should be limited to men of noble birth.
options.B: Parents should love their children, and children should obey their parents.
options.C: Husbands should fulfill their duties, and wives should be obedient.
options.D: Rulers should be kind to their subjects; subjects should be loyal to their rulers.

explanation_steps: The textbook: Confucius 'taught that government should not be limited to men of noble birth… government should be open to all men who have the wisdom and skill to govern.'
B, C and D are the Confucian duties of family and state relationships.
Answer: A.
tips: Confucius = order through proper relationships + government by the educated and able.

explanation_steps: The three Chinese philosophies were Confucianism, Taoism and Legalism.

options.A: The Church came to be known as the Eastern Orthodox Church.
options.B: The patriarch, and not the king, occupied a crucial position in the Empire.
options.C: The Byzantine Empire was both a Greek and Church state.

options.A: Agriculture was the basis of the Maya economy.
options.B: The Maya built splendid temples and developed a complicated calendar.
options.C: The Maya civilization flourished between 900-300 B.C. in the Yucatan Peninsula.

questions.stem: Identify the correct statement.

options.A: Over the period of two millennia the Bantu spread all over Sub-Saharan Africa.
options.B: Intermarriage was common among the African and Arab ruling groups.
options.C: Swahili combines Bantu and Arabic words and phrases.
options.D: The kingdom of Ghana was the first great trading state in West Africa as early as 500 B.C.

explanation_steps: A: textbook – 'Over a period of two millennia the Bantu spread almost all over sub-Saharan Africa.' True.

The examiner most probably intended E (D copies the textbook sentence with the era mistyped). Keyed E; A, B and C are each also accepted.

questions.stem: Why do Tigrean chiefs wanted to expand to Eritrea in the 18th and 19th centuries? (1 point)
questions.answer: Because controlling Eritrea would let them collect taxes and tribute from the Eritrean people, get access to the coast to obtain arms from abroad, and benefit from the Red Sea trade – which would help them become kings in Abyssinia. (Any one reason earns the point.)
explanation_steps: The textbook: the Tigrean lords 'believed that controlling Eritrea would help them achieve this [becoming kings]. They thought controlling Eritrea would: 1. enable them to collect taxes and tributes from the Eritrean people; 2. get them access to the coast and thereby enable them to obtain arms from abroad; 3. help them benefit from Red Sea trade.'
This is the same content as Part I Q17.
marking_points: 1 point: any one of – collect taxes/tribute; access to the coast to obtain arms; benefit from Red Sea trade (to become kings of Abyssinia)
tips: Same idea as Part I Q17 – the paper tests it twice.
